newsitem.title: USA: US LPGs rise in short coverings then reverse.
newsitem.headline: US LPGs rise in short coverings then reverse.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices went up early Monday and then reversed as the price of crude oil fell on the NYMEX.
Propane values in the Mont Belevieu, Texas, market were pegged at 35.00 and 35.50 cents a gallon, up a half cent from Friday. Deals were done at 35.25 and 35.50 cents a gallon.
Propane values in the Conway, Kansas, market held steady at 34.00/34.25 cents and material traded at 34.38 and 34.50 cents a gallon.
"I thought investors might wait for the API data to come out, but people seem to be cleaning up their July short positions," one player said.
Normal butane deals in the Belvieu hub were done at 40.25 and 40.75 cents a gallon. Normal values there went up a quarter cent to 40.25/40.50.
Other deals in Belvieu were made in isobutane at 43.75 cents per gallon, and in natural gasoline at 44 cents a gallon.
Natural gasoline went up a half cent in Conway to 43.75/44.00.
Both ethane purity and ethane mix went up a quarter cent in Belvieu, while ethane held steady in Conway.
One trader said, "Things opened positive today, but players were a little less enamored of making deals once the price of crude went down."
